page.layout: One printed page (left side of scan): one column of running text, with marginal notes in the left margin. Running head and page number at the top. Catchword at the lower right. A Greek couplet, then a Latin verse couplet, set as displayed quotations within the text. Right-hand strip is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.

main_text.p: erubuit, magiam Zoroastris nihil aliud esse, quàm divini cultus scientiam, quâ filios Persarum reges erudiebant, ut ad exemplar mundanæ Reip. suam ipsi regere remp. addiscerent. Idem in Epimonide Syris & Ægyptiis propter æstivi temporis in utraque regione serenitatem, ubi stellæ omnes clarè cernuntur, semper Astrologiæ tribuit inventionem, Syrumq; quempiam authorem nominum fuisse perhibet. Ægyptios quoq; præclaros fuisse philosophos, author est sanctus Stephanus Act. 7. v.22. ubi ait, Mosen institutum fuisse omni sapientiâ Ægyptiorum. Idipsum testatur Arist.1.Metaph. Manet igitur, Græcos illos, putà Pythagoram, Democritum, Apollonium, Tyanæum, Indorum quoq; Gymnosophistas & Brachmanes olim se contulisse ad Sapientes Orientales, Hebræos scilicet, Chaldæos & Ægyptios. Præterea Chaldæi & Hebræi etiam oraculo Delphico habiti sunt sapientissimi.

p.i: Μοῦνοι [?] χαλδαῖοι σοφὴν λέγον, οἱ δ' ἀρ' ἐβραῖοι
Chaldæi sapiunt soli, tum numen Hebræi Ingenitum, regemq; pio venerantur honore.

main_text.p: Peucerus tamen de divinat.generibus putat has fuisse diabolicas ironias. Quicquid huius sit, relinquitur, illos fuisse addictos philosophiæ: quamvis tractu temporis in ementitam sapientiam degenera-rint. Etsi autem optandum foret, Hebræorum philo-Rudera phi-losophiæ Hebræo-rum etiam hodie ex-tant.sophiam ad nos delatam esse; habemus tamen nihi-lominus illorum philosophiæ rudera, ut ita dicam, per manus nobis tradita. Ab Hebræis enim philosophia ad filios Hebræorum, Chaldæos, ab his ad vicinos Assyrios, & Ægyptios: inde ad Græcos pervenit, à

page.notes: Greek couplet: first word read as Μοῦνοι, the printed form may differ; "ἀνάγκῃ" and "σεβαζόμενοι" are doubtful in the scan. The Greek is copied as seen, not from a known source. The left margin note is printed at the line "sophiam ad nos delatam esse"; its hyphenated words are kept as printed. The scan has show-through and the neighbouring page's edge at the right, not transcribed.
